note: Anti-PD-1 antibodies entered SCLC with no SCLC model (nivolumab does not bind mouse PD-1, so the class relied on a surrogate antibody in generic syngeneic tumours plus cynomolgus toxicology); Rb1/Trp53 GEMM-derived SCLC mice arrived in 2019 and matched the clinic's weak single-agent activity, but the chemotherapy combinations that finally improved survival were never modelled.
label: SCLC (anti-PD-1)

engagement.model: Human T-cell assays and cynomolgus PD-1 binding (nivolumab; class-level, not SCLC)
engagement.note: Nivolumab binds human and cynomolgus PD-1 only; occupancy >70% was shown in other solid tumours (Brahmer 2010), never read out in SCLC.
engagement.short: Binds human/cyno PD-1; no SCLC read-out
engagement.quote: Nivolumab binds to PD-1 with high affinity and specificity, and effectively inhibits the interaction between PD-1 and its ligands.
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level reading (Cancer Immunol Res paywalled); the FDA 2014 pharmacology review corroborates binding to human and cynomolgus but not rodent PD-1. Engagement for the class was read out once in patients with melanoma, NSCLC, RCC, CRC and prostate cancer (Brahmer 2010, doi:10.1200/JCO.2009.26.7609: >70% PD-1 occupancy on circulating T cells at every dose); no SCLC trial measured engagement, so the context is untested rather than matched.

dose.model: Cynomolgus repeat-dose exposure margins (nivolumab; class-level, not SCLC)
dose.note: Monkey exposures at every dose exceeded the 3 mg/kg q2w clinical regimen; SCLC inherited that dose (later 240 mg flat) without an SCLC exposure-response test.
dose.short: Melanoma dose carried into SCLC untested
dose.quote: In both monkey studies, exposure of nivolumab at all dose levels tested exceeded that measured in humans at the intended clinical dose and schedule of 3 mg/kg once every 2 weeks.
dose.judgement: Read from the extracted review text (BLA 125554, memoranda dated 2014-12-04). The SCLC dose (CheckMate 032: 3 mg/kg q2w; 2018 SCLC label: 240 mg q2w) was carried over from receptor-occupancy and exposure-response work in other tumours; no SCLC-specific PK/PD comparison against any model was published, so untested.

efficacy.model: Generic syngeneic mouse tumours (MC38, CT26, SA1/N) with surrogate anti-mouse PD-1 antibody 4H2 (not SCLC)
efficacy.note: Nivolumab does not bind rodent PD-1; the class entered SCLC (CheckMate 032, 2013) on surrogate-antibody activity in colon and fibrosarcoma transplants, no SCLC model.
efficacy.quote: This murine surrogate for nivolumab exhibited anti-tumor activity in multiple murine syngeneic tumors models.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the strip with the model the class actually filed: the review states nivolumab does not recognize mouse PD-1 and that rat-derived clone 4H2 was used in MC38, CT26 and SA1/N transplants. No SCLC model was cited; the 2018 SCLC accelerated approval rested on CheckMate 032 clinical data only (FDA announcement 2018-08-16), which I did not verify against the supplement's review document.

efficacy.model: Rb1/Trp53(/p130) GEMM-derived syngeneic and autochthonous SCLC mice with surrogate anti-mouse PD-L1 (clone 10F.9G2)
efficacy.note: Single-agent checkpoint blockade did nothing in RPP flank and lung tumours; the paper sets this beside the ~10% ORR of anti-PD-1 monotherapy in CheckMate 032.
efficacy.short: Mouse SCLC inert to monotherapy, as patients
efficacy.quote: Single agent olaparib treatment had no significant anti-tumor activity and consistent with the previous observation, anti-PD-L1 alone had no anti-tumor effect in these models
efficacy.reason: Model and clinic agree: monotherapy inert
efficacy.judgement: Full text read from the PMC author manuscript (PMC6563834; the journal version may spell 'antitumor'). The same paper states the patient side: 'only a minority of SCLC patients respond to anti-PD-1 monotherapy or anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA4 combination (approximately 10% with monotherapy and 23% with the combination)', citing CheckMate 032 (Antonia 2016, doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(16)30098-5), so comparison_stated is true and the source calls it consistent. Three caveats drove 'same' rather than 'neg' or 'untested': (1) product_in_model is false twice over - a surrogate antibody, and an anti-PD-L1 one (Hiatt 2022, doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-22-1128, repeats the finding with an anti-PD-1 surrogate in the same Rb1/Trp53 syngeneic model, where PD-1 inhibition alone was weak and needed an LSD1 inhibitor); (2) the model was built after CheckMate 032 had reported, so the agreement is retrospective, and the later phase 3 monotherapy and maintenance failures (CheckMate 331, Spigel 2021, doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2021.01.071, OS HR 0.86, p=0.11; CheckMate 451, Owonikoko 2021, doi:10.1200/JCO.20.02212, HR 0.92, p=0.37) and the KEYNOTE-604 OS miss (Rudin 2020, doi:10.1200/JCO.20.00793, HR 0.80, p=0.0164 vs 0.0128 boundary) are my juxtaposition, not a model flag, so no 'neg'; (3) the regimen that did work, PD-1 antibody plus platinum-etoposide (ASTRUM-005 serplulimab, Cheng 2022, doi:10.1001/jama.2022.16464, OS HR 0.63; EXTENTORCH toripalimab 2025; RATIONALE-312 tislelizumab 2024), was never tested in SCLC mice, so the successful half of the class record is untested, not matched. Mahadevan 2021 (doi:10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-0913) links non-neuroendocrine MHC-I-high SCLC to durable ICB benefit in DFCI/CheckMate 032 patients but dosed no PD-1 antibody in mice, so it was not used as the comparison.

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 4- and 13-week repeat-dose toxicology (nivolumab binds cynomolgus PD-1)
safety.note: Monkeys tolerated up to 50 mg/kg with no immune-related adverse events, only diffuse inflammatory infiltrates; no target-organ toxicity identified.
safety.quote: Nivolumab treatment did not induce adverse immune-related events when given to cynomolgus macaques at high concentrations, independent of circulating anti-nivolumab antibodies where observed.
safety.judgement: Abstract-level reading; the FDA 2014 pharmacology review corroborates (well tolerated to 50 mg/kg, diffuse inflammatory infiltration, no target organ toxicity) and is the filed model.

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 4- and 13-week repeat-dose toxicology (nivolumab binds cynomolgus PD-1)
safety.note: Third-line nivolumab in SCLC: 55% treatment-related AEs, immune-related skin, pulmonary and neurologic events, one fatal pneumonitis; the monkey model had predicted none.
safety.short: Fatal pneumonitis the monkeys never showed
safety.quote: One treatment-related death due to pneumonitis was noted.
safety.judgement: Full text read (PMC8050700): nivolumab monotherapy, 109 SCLC patients, select (immunologic) TRAEs in skin (21.1%), grade 3-4 pneumonitis (1.8%), one grade 3-4 encephalitis and one pneumonitis death. The comparison with the monkey data is mine (comparison_stated false); Ready 2019 does not mention nonclinical work, and Wang 2014 frames clinical safety as 'demonstrated', so source_calls_it is null. The FDA 2014 review itself places 'autoimmune disturbances are the most commonly reported adverse events' directly after the clean monkey findings, but in melanoma patients, outside this context. Earlier SCLC signal: Antonia 2016 (doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(16)30098-5) reported treatment-related deaths from myasthenia gravis, renal failure and pneumonitis, all in nivolumab plus ipilimumab arms, so I anchored the year on the monotherapy cohort; a reviewer preferring 2016 can move it. Monkeys did show diffuse inflammatory infiltrates without organ toxicity, a partial signal the status does not credit.
